Narrative from partner:
In June, Keystone continued to provide countrywide targeted support to refugees in Moldova, with particular attention to persons with disabilities and other individuals facing heightened vulnerability. Assistance was closely linked to the case management and needs assessment process, with targeted outreach focusing especially on persons referred through the Hotline. During the reporting period, 11 detailed needs assessment questionnaires were completed, allowing the team to better understand beneficiaries’ individual situations, identify priority needs, and plan tailored follow-up support based on the specific challenges reported by each person or family.
Based on the assessed needs, Keystone continued the distribution of non-food items and the provision of medical and related support services. In June, 28 people benefited from such assistance, bringing the cumulative number of beneficiaries reached to 156 out of the revised target of 138 people. This progress reflects both the continuation of support provided in previous months and the additional assistance delivered during June, when 18 unique beneficiaries were reached. The support provided during the month included hygiene supplies for 18 people, assistive devices for 7 people, and medical equipment for 3 people, ensuring that assistance responded to concrete functional, health-related, and basic support needs.
In addition to planned support, several urgent cases referred by UNHCR were assisted during the reporting period. These interventions required prompt coordination, individualized follow-up, and rapid linkage with appropriate forms of assistance to ensure that beneficiaries with acute needs were not left without support. Through this combined approach, Keystone was able to connect emergency referrals with practical assistance while maintaining continuity between assessment, case follow-up, and service response.

Narrative from partner:
During April 2026, CCR started implementing specialised GBV awareness and prevention activities for refugee and asylum seeker women at the CCR Community Centre and at the Protection Hub within the Temporary Accommodation Centre (TAC) in Chișinău.

The sessions focused on the topic “Power, Control, and Roles in Relationships” and aimed to increase awareness regarding healthy and unhealthy relationship dynamics, emotional well-being, personal boundaries, gender roles, and protection-related risks. The activities also provided a safe space for discussion, information sharing, and psychosocial support for women in vulnerable situations.

The following sessions were conducted during the reporting period:

1. GBV Session: “Power, Control, and Roles in Relationships”
CCR Community Centre, Chișinău – 22 April 2026
2. GBV Session: “Power, Control, and Roles in Relationships”
CCR Community Centre, Chișinău – 24 April 2026
3. Lecture on GBV: “Power, Control, and Roles in Relationships”
CCR Community Centre, Chișinău – 27 April 2026
4. GBV Session: “Power, Control, and Roles in Relationships”
CCR Community Centre, Chișinău – 29 April 2026
5. GBV Session: “Power, Control, and Roles in Relationships”
CCR Community Centre, Chișinău – 30 April 2026
6. GBV Session: “Power, Control, and Roles in Relationships”
Protection Hub, Temporary Accommodation Centre, Dacia 60/4, Chișinău – 30 April 2026

In total, 6 GBV sessions were conducted during April 2026, reaching 87 women participants. The activities contributed to strengthening awareness, protection, psychosocial well-being, and access to information for refugee and asylum seeker women.

Narrative from partner:
In February 2026, CCR delivered 14 psychological support activities at the CCR Community Centre in Chișinău and at the Protection Hub within the Temporary Accommodation Centre (TAC). Services included individual psychological counselling, group psychoeducational sessions, and community-based wellbeing activities, addressing topics such as fear of mistakes, perfectionism, emotional resilience, personal development and future planning. Activities also included Women’s Club meetings combining creative workshops and facilitated psychological discussions, as well as structured techniques such as neurographica and guided drawing exercises used as therapeutic tools for emotional expression and stress management. These sessions provided a safe and supportive environment for refugees, asylum seekers and persons under temporary protection to discuss challenges, strengthen coping strategies and enhance psychosocial wellbeing.
Art therapy sessions were not conducted in February as the responsible specialist was on medical leave during this period.
In total: 
71 beneficiaries, 26 are new.
14 psychological sessions

Narrative from partner:
In May, Keystone continued the distribution of non-food items to support refugee communities in Moldova, with particular attention to persons facing heightened vulnerability. Targeted outreach focused on individuals referred through the Hotline, and 31 detailed needs assessment questionnaires were completed during the reporting period, enabling the team to identify priority needs and tailor follow-up assistance accordingly.
Medical and related support services reached 26 people in May, bringing the cumulative number of beneficiaries served to 128 out of the revised target of 138 people. Following the project extension, the overall target was increased from 69 to 138 beneficiaries. This progress builds on assistance provided in previous months, including 18 unique beneficiaries reached in May and 93 beneficiaries served overall. During the month, 17 people received hygiene supplies, 4 were provided with assistive devices, and 4 received medical equipment. In addition, 1 child completed rehabilitation services, while 2 wheelchairs were distributed through UNHCR support.
Several urgent cases referred by UNHCR were also assisted during May. These interventions required prompt coordination and individualized follow-up to ensure that beneficiaries with acute needs were connected to appropriate support and received timely assistance.

GBV session:

1 Group Session: "The Concept of Gender-Based Violence (GBV) and Markers of Unhealthy Relationships" – CCR Community Centre, Chișinău – 6 May 2026

A specialized awareness-raising and prevention session on GBV was conducted for refugee and asylum-seeking women. The session introduced the basic concepts of GBV and explored the differences between conflict and abusive behaviour, including physical, psychological, and economic violence.
Participants discussed the characteristics of healthy relationships based on mutual respect, equality, and partnership, as well as warning signs of unhealthy relationships involving control, coercion, and emotional manipulation. The session also addressed common myths and misconceptions related to domestic violence and provided information on available protection and support services.

Number of participants: 20

I. Romanian language classes

CCR continued implementing Romanian language classes for refugees, asylum seekers, and host community members through several educational initiatives conducted at the CCR Community Centre, online platforms, and partner educational institutions.

1. Romanian language classes at the CCR Community Centre

Teacher: Natalia Buga
Two groups (A1 and A2 levels) continued attending Romanian language classes at the CCR Community Centre twice per week, with sessions lasting 1.5 hours each:

A1 group: Tuesday and Thursday, 10:00–11:30
A2 group: Tuesday and Thursday, 14:30–16:00

In total, 48 unique beneficiaries attended the classes during May 2026, 12 new participants joined the classes.

2. Romanian language classes implemented in cooperation with the “Ion Creangă” State Pedagogical University

Teacher: Alexandra Munteanu
Two A1-level groups continued functioning during the reporting period:

- one offline group at the CCR Community Centre;
- one online group.

In total, 49 unique beneficiaries attended both groups during May 2026, no new participants.

3. Romanian language classes at the “Ion Creangă” State Pedagogical University

Teacher: Ana Cozari
Two A1-level groups were conducted:

- one offline group at the university premises;
- one online group.

In total, 30 unique beneficiaries attended both groups during May 2026, no new participants.

5. Romanian language classes in Russian-language schools for refugee children

Romanian language classes for refugee children continued in seven Russian-language educational institutions across Moldova. During May 2026, the following numbers of children attended the classes:

A. Chekhov Theoretical Lyceum – 49 students (22 boys, 27 girls), aged 7–16 years.
N. Gogol Theoretical Lyceum – 40 students (21 boys, 19 girls), aged 7–16 years.
M. Lomonosov Theoretical Lyceum – 47 students (21 boys, 26 girls), aged 7–16 years.
T. Shevchenko Gymnasium – 40 students (17 boys, 23 girls), aged 7–16 years.
D. Mavrodi Theoretical Lyceum (Comrat) – 41 students (23 boys, 18 girls), aged 7–16 years.
Gloria Theoretical Lyceum of Sports Profile (LTPS Gloria) – 40 students (23 boys, 17 girls), aged 7–16 years.
A. Pushkin Theoretical Lyceum (Anenii Noi) – 40 students (19 boys, 21 girls), aged 7–16 years.

Total: 297 students (146 boys and 151 girls) attended Romanian language classes during the reporting period. 5 new individuals.

II. Support for the inclusion of refugees and asylum seekers’ children in the national education system

During the reporting period, CCR continued providing consultations, guidance, and individual support to refugee and asylum seeker families regarding access to education and inclusion within the Moldovan national education system.

Support included counselling related to school enrolment procedures, communication with educational institutions, orientation regarding available educational opportunities, and assistance in addressing practical barriers affecting children’s participation in education.

36 newly identified cases requiring enrolment support were registered during April 2026.

III. Beneficiaries of literacy classes for Roma children and adolescents

CCR continued implementing literacy classes for Roma refugee and local children and adolescents in four locations across Moldova within the framework of the UNHCR-supported programme.

Number of enrolled children:

1) RAC Popeasca – 12 children (3 girls, 9 boys)
4 local children
8 refugee children

2) Bender, Transnistrian region – 13 children (9 girls, 4 boys)
6 refugee children
7 local children

3) RAC Nisporeni – 14 children (6 girls, 5 boys, 3 women)
all refugee children

4) Soroca, “D. Matcovschi” Gymnasium – 17 children (9 girls, 8 boys)
all local children

At present, the literacy programme includes a total of 56 beneficiaries.

During May 2026, CCR conducted monitoring visits and assessment of challenges in all four programme locations:

18 May 2026 – Popeasca;
19 May 2026 – Niporeni;
20 May 2026 – Bender;
26 May 2026 – Soroca.

The Roma Project Coordinator also participated in the Refugee Education Working Group (REWG) meeting held on 28 May 2026 at the UNHCR office in Chișinău.

Several operational and protection-related challenges were identified during the reporting period.

Two new Roma families were accommodated at the Nisporeni Accommodation Centre. One of the families has four children, with a fifth child expected soon. The children, aged 10, 8, and 7, have never attended school despite having lived in the Republic of Moldova for approximately one year.

With the completion of our literacy project and the partnership activities implemented by TARNA ROM and UNHCR, there is a risk that outreach and engagement with the Roma community may become more challenging. We therefore express concern regarding the continuity of school enrolment for Roma children, as well as the provision of ongoing support to ensure their participation in the 2026–2027 academic year.


In total - 480 beneficiaries participated in education activities, out of which 53 are new beneficiaries.

These included individual counselling sessions and group activities such as the Women’s Club session on “Control and Perfectionism: From the Pursuit of Perfection to Accepting ‘Good Enough’” and a neurographic art practice session (“Neuro Tree of Desires”).

2. Art therapy sessions:
A total of 10 sessions were conducted, reaching 105 beneficiaries. Activities included drawing, right-brain creative exercises, crafting (soft toys, knitting), and a cooking masterclass, implemented at both CCR and TAC.

Narrative from partner:
During the reporting period, 5 Ukrainian refugees with medical backgrounds were engaged as Health Mediators to support access to healthcare for Ukrainian nationals under Temporary Protection (TP) in the Republic of Moldova. Through their outreach activities, IOM Health Mediators conducted 29 community-level information sessions, reaching a total of 843 individuals (175 male and 668 female). The sessions focused on improving beneficiaries’ awareness and understanding of the Moldovan healthcare system, including its structure, functioning, and the procedures required to access primary and specialized medical services.
In addition to awareness-raising activities, Health Mediators provided individualized support to facilitate access to primary healthcare. As a result, 93 individuals under TP were successfully registered with a Family Doctor during the reporting period, strengthening their access to healthcare services.

2026 Project Reporting Form Project/Acti: Suportul prin linie telefonică și echipa mobilă pentru comunitățile de refugiați din Moldova
Sector - outcome area Outcome area: Legal Framework, Legal Status, Access to Territory, Asylum and to Justice
Activity 2026 Activity: Provide comprehensive protection assistance and case management services to refugees, including individualized support for vulnerable cases, while conducting targeted awareness-raising campaigns on protection risks and rights
Indicators 2026 Indicator 2026: # of individuals with specific needs receiving targeted protection support/assistance
Narrative from partner:
A1. Provision of Informational Support through the 24/7 National Helpline
Keystone provided 24/7 informational support through the National Helpline. In Q1, 52 calls were recorded in total (22 in January; 16 in February and 14 in March). 
•	Gender (Jan–Feb): 30 female, 8 male.
•	Vulnerability profile (Jan–March): 27 persons with disabilities, 12 persons with chronic diseases, and 11 persons without a disability degree; 2 children with dissabilities.
•	Main caller locations: Anenii Noi, Bălți, Cantemir, Chișinău, Dondușeni, Glodeni (January); Chișinău, Cahul, Bălți, Hîncești.
•	Call data was used to identify priority needs and inform referrals and targeted interventions for vulnerable refugees.
•	Main requests: hygiene products in the form of diapers, assistive equipment in the form of a walker, toilet seat, bath chair, cane; Medical equipment: tonometer, glucometer; Medical examinations for children and adults diagnosed with cancer; financial resources for paying rent; Food and clothing; Psychological support for panic attacks, anxiety, physical and psychological overwork, depressive states with isolation; Rehabilitation services for children with ASD; Request for support to be able to undergo eye surgery.
•	Request for information on: How to access primary and specialized medical services; Information on the package of documents and the procedure for determining the degree of disability in the Republic of Moldova; Access to medical problems for people with mental health; Procedure for obtaining temporary protection; Request for living space

A2. Countrywide Targeted Support to Persons with Disabilities Based on Case Management and Needs Assessment
Keystone delivered countrywide targeted support to persons with disabilities through case management and needs assessments, linking helpline referrals to timely NFI distribution, medical services, and rehabilitation support. In Q1, 66 needs assessments were completed (15 in January; 16 in February; 35 in March).
•	Medical services: 25 individuals supported in February and 45 in March (Q1 total ~70 services), reaching 53 cumulative unique medical beneficiaries by end of March.
•	Hygiene items: 19 individuals supported in February and 24 in March (Q1 total 43 individuals).
•	Assistive devices: 2 distributed in February and 8 in March (Q1 total 10), improving mobility and independence.
•	Medical equipment: 4 items supplied in February and 11 in March (Q1 total 15).
•	Rehabilitation for children: 2 children started sessions in February and completed in March; 4 additional children started in March with completion planned for mid-April.
•	Operational readiness: questionnaire updated in January; three Price Offer Competitions (RTO) initiated to identify medical service suppliers.
A3. Information Outreach & Advocacy
Keystone strengthened information outreach and disability inclusion advocacy by maintaining technical support on accessibility information, disseminating disability mapping findings to coordination forums, and advancing multi-stakeholder engagement through the Disability & Age Technical Group (DATF) and a planned round table with authorities and partners.
•	Maintained ongoing technical assistance to ensure accessibility information remained available to refugee communities.
•	Prepared and then delivered presentations of the disability mapping exercise findings (presented at the PWG in March) to support gap analysis and prioritization.
•	Round table advocacy event: initiated preparations in January; rescheduled to April; agenda, invitation letters, and an action-plan matrix finalized in March.
•	Conducted mapping of service providers supporting refugees with disabilities and older adults to strengthen referral pathways and coordination.
•	Co-chaired the DATF with UNHCR, contributing to the 2025–2026 Refugee Response Plan Year-End/Mid-Term Report; updated member/contact lists and submitted the group’s Terms of Reference and Work Plans.
•	Participatory Assessment: held 2 focus group discussions in Chișinău with refugees with disabilities, covering legal stay status (including post-Temporary Protection planning) and inclusion/integration issues.

Event no. 1: Information session and Easter celebration with distribution of Easter cakes
CCR organised an information and community event dedicated to the celebration of Easter at the CCR Community Centre in Chișinău on 14 April 2026. The activity brought together refugee families and vulnerable beneficiaries in a welcoming and community-oriented environment.
During the event, beneficiaries received information and participated in discussions aimed at strengthening community engagement and social inclusion. In parallel, Easter cakes were distributed to vulnerable refugee families as part of the seasonal support activities.
A total of 223 beneficiaries participated in the event and benefited from the distribution, with one Easter cake provided per family. The activity contributed to fostering community cohesion, maintaining cultural traditions, and supporting the emotional well-being of refugee families during the holiday period.

Event no. 2: Information session and Easter celebration with distribution of Easter cakes

On 16 April 2026, CCR organised an information session and Easter celebration at the Protection Hub hosted within the Temporary Accommodation Centre (TAC) in Chișinău. The event brought together asylum seekers and refugees residing in the TAC in a supportive and community-oriented environment.

The activity combined community engagement, information sharing, and seasonal support, contributing to the emotional well-being and social inclusion of beneficiaries during the Easter period. Easter cakes were distributed to participating families and individuals as part of the celebration.

A total of 38 beneficiaries participated in the event and benefited from the activity and distribution support.

Events no. 3, 4, 5 and 6: International Roma Day cultural activities

On the occasion of International Roma Day, annually marked on 8 April, CCR colleagues involved in the Roma Literacy Classes programme funded by UNHCR Moldova organised a series of cultural and educational activities for Roma refugee and local children in several locations across Moldova.

The activities took place:

1. on 8 April 2026 in Soroca (Matcovschi Gymnasium): 17 beneficiaries.
2. on 8 April 2026 in Popeasca: 13 beneficiaries.
3. on 8 April 2026 in Bender (School No. 7): 13 beneficiaries.
4. on 9 April 2026 in Nisporeni: 11 beneficiaries.

The events aimed to promote awareness and appreciation of Roma culture, traditions, and identity, while fostering diversity, inclusion, tolerance, and mutual respect among children from refugee and host communities. Through interactive activities, discussions, and cultural elements, the initiative encouraged positive social interaction and community cohesion in the participating localities.

Event no. 7: Participation in the event dedicated to the Day of Motherhood and Beauty organised by the Armenian community in Moldova

On 7 April 2026, CCR participated in the event dedicated to the Day of Motherhood and Beauty, organised by the Armenian community in the Republic of Moldova under the leadership of Venera Gasparyan. The event brought together representatives of the Parliament of the Republic of Moldova, public institutions, international organisations, civil society organisations, community leaders, and members of different ethnic communities.

During the event, CCR representatives had the opportunity to present the organisation’s activities and programmes implemented with the support of UNHCR Moldova, highlighting culturally sensitive approaches to refugee inclusion and community engagement. Particular emphasis was placed on the active participation of different ethnic and refugee communities within CCR programmes, including educational, cultural, and integration activities promoting diversity, intercultural dialogue, and social cohesion.

The event served as an important platform for strengthening intercultural communication, promoting mutual respect, and recognising the contribution of ethnic communities to Moldova’s social and cultural life.

Approximately 500 participants attended the event, including both refugees - 35 participants and host community members - 465 participants. 

The activity contributed to promoting inclusion, peaceful coexistence, and stronger collaboration between refugee and host communities in Moldova.

Event no. 8: Participation in the inauguration of the “Friendship Alley” initiative

On 4 April 2026, a representative group from the Charity Centre for Refugees (CCR), led by the organisation’s Director, Mr. Djavid Paknehad, participated in the inauguration event of the “Friendship Alley”, an initiative launched by the Chișinău Municipality to promote unity, diversity, and peaceful coexistence among communities.

The event brought together representatives of different nationalities and communities, including participants from Moldova, Ukraine, Afghanistan, Sudan, Libya, and France. Through its participation, CCR promoted intercultural dialogue, mutual respect, solidarity, and the inclusion of refugees within the social and community life of Chișinău.

The activity also provided an opportunity to highlight the importance of community-based initiatives that encourage positive interaction between refugees and host communities, while fostering a sense of belonging and social cohesion.

Approximately 100 individuals were present during the event, including both refugees and members of the host community.
The event contributed to strengthening social cohesion, promoting inclusion and diversity, and encouraging positive engagement between refugee and host communities in Moldova.

Overall, a total of 915 individuals, including refugees, asylum seekers, and members of the host community from Moldova, benefited from the community, cultural, and social cohesion activities implemented and supported by CCR during the reporting period. These activities contributed to strengthening intercultural dialogue, promoting inclusion and diversity, encouraging community participation, and fostering positive interaction between refugee and host communities across different localities in Moldova.

At present, the literacy programme includes a total of 55 beneficiaries.

During April 2026, CCR conducted monitoring visits and assessment of challenges in all four programme locations:

2 April – Popeasca
9 April – Nisporeni
22 April – Soroca
27 April – Bender

Several operational and protection-related challenges were identified during the reporting period.

A major challenge was reported in Bender, where School No. 7, previously hosting the literacy classes for Roma children, was closed. The children were transferred to School No. 16, where some children reportedly experienced bullying, discrimination, and conflicts within the educational environment. As a temporary solution, the literacy classes supported by UNHCR were moved online, since the new school administration did not approve continuation of the activities on school premises during the remaining school period.

Another challenge was identified in Nisporeni, where the administration of the dormitory hosting both refugee families and students restricted refugees’ access to one of the educational spaces previously used for classes. Following discussions conducted by CCR staff, temporary permission was obtained to continue conducting the classes in the respective space until 31 May 2026.

CCR also continued follow-up on vulnerable displaced Roma families relocated from RAC Bulboaca to other localities. Despite communication difficulties with one relocated family, CCR managed to confirm that four school-aged children had been enrolled in a Romanian-language educational institution. Additionally, two Roma children displaced from RAC Bulboaca were successfully enrolled in the gymnasium in Cărpineni, Hîncești district, where they currently attend classes regularly.

During the reporting period, CCR and its partners also marked the International Roma Culture and Traditions Week through thematic educational and cultural activities organised across all four programme locations, promoting inclusion, cultural identity, diversity, and social cohesion among Roma refugee and host community children.

Grand total - 113 new beneficiaries.

Romanian classes

In January 2026, Romanian language classes were held at the CCR Community Centre twice per week (Tuesday and Thursday, 10:00–11:30). A total of 24 unique adult beneficiaries attended the course. On 29 January 2026, participants successfully passed the final Romanian language evaluation test, completing the course.

CCR continued Romanian language classes for refugee children enrolled in Russian-language instruction schools to support their linguistic integration. In January, courses were attended by 162 students aged 7–16, including 86 boys and 76 girls, in the following institutions: LT N. Gogol – 40 students (21 boys, 19 girls); Gymnasium T. Șevcenco – 40 students (17 boys, 23 girls); LT D. Mavrodi, Comrat – 42 students (25 boys, 17 girls); LTPS Gloria – 40 students (23 boys, 17 girls). Romanian classes in LT A. Cehov, LT M. Lomonosov and LT A. Pușkin (Anenii Noi) were scheduled but had not yet started in January.

Location 3 – Ion Creangă State Pedagogical University, Chișinău
Romanian language courses were also conducted at the Ion Creangă State Pedagogical University, facilitated by teacher Ana Cozari. In January, two groups participated: an offline group with 19 learners and an online group with 20 learners, for a total of 39 participants attending Romanian language lessons.

In total for Romanian language classes: 233

Narrative from partner:
I. Art-Therapy.
In January 2026, CCR provided 12 group Art-Therapy sessions, implemented at the CCR Community Centre in Chișinău, the Protection Hub at the Temporary Accommodation Centre (Dacia 60/4), and the RefugeeAccommodation Centres in Cărpineni and Criuleni. Activities included art-therapy drawing sessions, right-brain drawing workshops, women’s club meetings and a culinary master-class, offering beneficiaries safe spaces for emotional expression, stress relief, peer support and community interaction. In total, 166 unique beneficiaries participated in these MHPSS group activities, contributing to improved psychosocial wellbeing and social connectedness among refugees and displaced persons supported by CCR.

II. Psychological support (group and individual)
In January 2026, CCR delivered 11 psychological support activities combining group sessions, individual counselling, psychoeducational workshops and wellbeing-oriented creative practices at the CCR Community Centre in Chișinău and the Community Centre in Cărpineni. The activities focused on emotional self-regulation, anxiety reduction, stress resilience, sharing coping strategies, and strengthening peer support within the refugee community, including sessions integrated with the Romanian language course for beneficiaries. Individual psychological consultations were also provided to address personal emotional and psychosocial needs. In total, 141 unique beneficiaries participated in these psychological support activities, contributing to improved emotional wellbeing, resilience and community connection among refugees and displaced persons supported by CCR.

The majority of refugees, asylum seekers and persons under temporary protection supported during the reporting period originated from Ukraine, with a smaller number coming from Afghanistan, Cuba, Azerbaijan, Tajikistan, the Russian Federation, Gaza/Palestine and Moldova (stateless persons).

Activity 2026 Activity: Promote social cohesion and foster community support between refugees and host communities through joint initiatives, with a focus on building mutual understanding and resilience
Indicators 2026 Indicator 2026: # of individuals benefitting from social cohesion activities and community-based initiatives
Narrative from partner:
During June 2026, CCR organised or participated in seven community events promoting inclusion, social cohesion, children’s rights, cultural exchange, and solidarity:

1. International Children’s Day event, Botanical Garden, Chișinău – 1 June 2026: approximately 500 children reached through games, animation, mascot activities, and distribution of refreshments.

2. International Children’s Day celebration, Early Childhood Rehabilitation Centre, Chișinău – 1 June 2026: 130 children.

3. iProsop Festival, Selemet, Cimișlia district: approximately 500 participants reached through recreational activities, animation, and refreshments.

4. Presentation of two bilingual Romanian–Ukrainian children’s books, CCR Community Centre – 10 June 2026: 23 participants.

5. Voluntary Blood Donation Campaign marking World Refugee Day, CCR Community Centre – 17 June 2026: 113 participants.

6. World Refugee Day celebration, Temporary Accommodation Centre, Chișinău – 19 June 2026: more than 150 refugees, asylum seekers, and host-community members.

7. Information session and celebration of the traditional Moldovan blouse, “Ziua Iei”, CCR Community Centre – 24 June 2026: 30 participants.

Total individuals reached: at least 1,446 participants, out of which - 1391 new.

Activity 2026 Activity: Provide MHPSS and recreational activities

Sector - outcome area Outcome area: Equitable Access to Quality and Inclusive Education
Activity 2026 Activity: Provision of non-formal education for refugee and vulnerable Moldovan children and adolescents
Indicators 2026 Indicator 2026: # of refugee and vulnerable Moldovan children and adolescents benefiting from summer camps, recreational and social cohesion activities organized in schools
Narrative from partner: Under this activity, refugee and vulnerable Moldovan children and adolescents benefited from summer camps, recreational activities, and social cohesion initiatives organized in schools across the following locations: Chisinau, Bălți, Soroca, Comrat, Orhei, Ungheni, Criuleni, Edineț, Fălești, Basarabeasca, and Anenii Noi. These activities aimed to promote inclusion, well-being, peer interaction, and social cohesion between refugee and host community children. Sex and age disaggregated data (SADD) will be available in the next reporting period, as participant registration is currently being implemented through a database system.

2026 Project Reporting Form Project/Acti: Moldova Red Cross Society  humanitarian response 2025
Sector - outcome area Outcome area: Inclusive Social Protection Systems, Economic Empowerment and Labor Market Integration
Activity 2026 Activity: Deliver targeted Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance to vulnerable refugees to meet their essential needs and reduce protection risks
Indicators 2026 Indicator 2026: # of vulnerable individuals supported with cash assistance for winter related needs
Narrative from partner:
Under the cash assistance component, 480 Ukrainian beneficiaries and 480 host community beneficiaries were supported as vulnerable individuals receiving cash assistance for winter-related needs. Each family received a one-time cash transfer of 1,840 MDL through MoneyGram. The assistance will be provided in Chisinau, Bălți, Soroca, Comrat, Orhei, Ungheni, Criuleni, Edineț, Fălești, Basarabeasca, and Anenii Noi.

In Chișinău, Briceni and Drochia a total of 2,000 vouchers were distributed to 1,000 beneficiaries. Each voucher had a value of 460 MDL and could be redeemed at Linella. Each beneficiary received two vouchers, with a total value of 920 MDL per person.
Project/Activity Title: Moldova Red Cross Society  humanitarian response 2025
